summary: P0: Elevated 5xx and streaming disconnects caused by connection-pool starvation during synchronous model hot-swap
description:
Issue summary: BrightVoice.ai reported a sudden rise in 5xx errors (502/503) and streaming session disconnects starting 2026-03-13 09:12 UTC. Errors coincided with an automated synchronous model hot-swap initiated by the scheduler for a dedicated pool. Impact: multiple customer routes experienced elevated error rates, degraded streaming reliability, and increased tail latency for ~18 minutes. Customer-facing SLA impact observed for a subset of enterprise tenants.

Observed behavior: - API gateway returned 502/503 to clients during streaming handshakes and short-lived generation requests. - Runtime logs show repeated 'connection pool exhausted' and 'upstream reset' messages at the time of the hot-swap. - A spike in pending connections and accept-queue depth was visible on the edge during swap window.

Business impact: BrightVoice.ai reported failed transcription requests and aborted streaming sessions. Estimated error-rate increase: 8% -> 24% for affected routes during the window.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) On a dedicated pool with active streaming traffic, trigger a synchronous model hot-swap (scheduler-controlled).
2) Maintain moderate concurrent streaming sessions (200-600 concurrent connections).
3) Observe gateway logs and client session behavior during the swap window.
Expected: warm handoff with minimal disruption. Actual: elevated 5xx, streaming disconnects, and increased accept queue leading to connection pool exhaustion.
logs_and_signals: - apigw logs (us-east) showing surge of 502/503 between 2026-03-13T09:12:05Z and 2026-03-13T09:30:20Z. - runtime logs: 'ERROR connection_pool: no available connections' repeated ~1300x. - scheduler audit: 'hot-swap start' and 'hot-swap complete' timestamps correlate to error window. - metrics: accept_queue_depth peaked at 147 (baseline ~12), idle_worker_count dropped, kernel evictions increased. - network: no upstream network packet drops on infra level; TLS handshakes had higher latency but completed.
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: model reload caused per-runtime thread spike and temporarily reduced available upstream proxies; apigw ingress accepted connections faster than proxies could drain.
- Observed that hot-swap path used synchronous drain + immediate restart on the same worker group instead of staggered replacement. This caused a transient connection pool under-provisioning.
- Verified KV cache warmup was blocking in some runtimes during reload, increasing CPU and blocking accept handlers.
- Confirmed no GPU OOMs, but runtime process thread pools were at capacity due to KV lock contention.
- Cross-checked scheduler logs: concurrent hot-swaps for 3 shards were initiated within 20s window due to a backfilled rollout job.
- Temporary mitigation (rollback) executed by Eng at 09:31Z which reduced errors.
comments: 2026-03-13 09:20 - Support (Ava): Customer reported intermittent 502s and dropped streams. Collected logs and escalated to SRE.
2026-03-13 09:24 - SRE (Ravi): Observed connection_pool exhaustion messages on runtime. Opening investigation. Noted scheduler hot-swap at 09:12.
2026-03-13 09:29 - Eng (Maya): Scheduler initiated 3 near-simultaneous shard swaps. Suggest immediate rollback of in-flight swap to reduce pressure.
2026-03-13 09:31 - Eng (Ravi): Rolled back hot-swap. Error rate decreasing. Informing customer and monitoring.
2026-03-13 10:05 - Support (Ava): BrightVoice.ai confirmed services recovered; requested postmortem and preventive measures.
current_status_update: Mitigation applied (rollback of hot-swap) at 2026-03-13T09:31Z. Error rate returned to baseline by 2026-03-13T09:40Z. Monitoring in place for any recurrence. Dedicated pool flagged for staggered swap policy enforcement.
root_cause: Concurrent synchronous hot-swaps across multiple shards led to temporary under-provisioning of upstream connections. Synchronous drain/restart behaviour combined with KV cache warmup blocking increased runtime thread saturation, exhausting connection pools and causing apigw 502/503 responses.
resolution:
Short term: Rolled back hot-swap and re-routed traffic to warm workers; increased ephemeral connection pool size for the affected dedicated pool.
Long term: Scheduler change to enforce staggered model hot-swap (max 1 shard per window), add pre-warm async model load path to reduce KV cache blocking, and increase apigw accept-queue backpressure thresholds for dedicated pools.
post_incident_actions:
- Owners: scheduler team (Ravi), serving-runtime (Maya).
- Action: Implement 'staggered hot-swap' gating and add canary checks for accept_queue depth before initiating swaps. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Action: Instrument KV cache warmup latency per-shard to prevent blocking accept handlers. ETA: 1 week.
- Action: Add an automated safeguard to temporarily reject new swaps when accept_queue_depth > 50. ETA: 3 days.
next_steps: 1) Create INT ticket for scheduler rollout gating (linked). 2) Schedule follow-up meeting with BrightVoice.ai CS on 2026-03-16 to review mitigations and timeline. 3) Deploy apigw temporary connection pool increase for affected dedicated pools this afternoon.
estimated_customer_impact_summary: BrightVoice.ai: ~18 minutes of elevated error rates for streaming and short-generation routes, ~15% of active sessions impacted during window. No data loss reported; best-effort retries allowed recovery for most clients.
customer_communication: Support sent an initial incident notification at 2026-03-13T10:10Z acknowledging the disruption, summarizing mitigation, and promising a post-incident report. Customer requested root-cause and timeline for fixes.
